question: Do proximal and distal within-species gene-level recurrence separately exceed the existing measurement-matched expectation?
status: Exploratory follow-up requested after inspecting aggregate recurrence and directional counts.
directional_recurrence: At least two studies with event -1 (proximal) or +1 (distal); one study vote requires agreement across every measurable series. An opposing third study is allowed, as in the original analysis.
null_model: Existing L3_full strata and frozen event labels; permute labels independently within each study and stratum. Preserve gene observability, eligible-study count, exact measurable-series combination, directional capacity, expression and APA-coverage terciles, reference-DWUI quintile and PAS-number tercile.
seed: Replay the original seed: 20261003 + first 12 hexadecimal SHA-256 digits of recurrence_control|species|contrast|threshold|L3_full.
primary_test: One-sided count enrichment: (1 + number of null counts >= observed)/(10000 + 1).
multiple_testing: BH across eight directional count tests at 0.02; separate eight-test BH at 0.05. Also report joint BH across all 16 as a sensitivity.
secondary_question: Is the distal fraction among recurrent genes shifted relative to the same matched null?
secondary_test: Distal/(proximal+distal), with two-sided equal-tail permutation P = min(1, 2*min(P_lower,P_upper)); BH across four contexts per threshold, with joint eight-test BH also reported. This tests directional composition, separately from directional count enrichment.
verification: Primary ladder and recurrent roster match the current 9 October source-data archive by SHA-256.
Reviewed numerical source hashes match the original recurrence-controls audit.
Frozen inputs and observed directional memberships reproduce the published roster at both thresholds.
Proximal plus distal null counts equal the original saved total recurrence count in every one of the 10000 draws for every context.
Permutation means agree with analytic expectations computed from within-stratum event probabilities.
Intent tests cover an opposing third study, missing study votes, preserved event margins and analytic null expectations.
scope_boundary: No new PAS calling, state assignment, recurrence selection, cross-species test or manuscript revision. Direction refers to a change in gene-wide relative PAS position; it does not establish absolute PAS preference, UTR-length change or function.
